summary: Every lesson from the three prior re-records is applied and verifies: the lead target is fenced and occurs exactly once, all four harness identifiers are quoted complete rather than truncated, the condition-2 block preserves all three prior rows' remainders and adds DR-123's, and the counts close at thirty against my own tally. I also suspected the shared CONSENT digest between D-008 and D-009 was a copy-paste error and it is not — both belong to the same four-entry batch review whose turn-3 verdict is cd08c5f0. One defect stands. DR-123's status cell routes evidence to DR-G17, the entry's own recitation quotes that text and explains why G17 is inapplicable after D-077, and clause 4 then contains zero edits to it. The row would go SATISFIED asserting an evidence route to a dropped gate in one cell while the neighbouring cell this entry writes says that gate is inapplicable.

objections.location: Subject, Decision clause 4 — the DR-123 status cell tail 'evidence at DR-G01..G05/G12/G17', and secondarily the source-pin column's 'DR-114/122; DR-G01–G05/G12/G17'
objections.claim: The entry records SATISFIED into a cell whose next clause routes evidence to DR-G17, a gate D-077 dropped, and specifies no edit to it — while adding a statement to the same row that G17 is inapplicable.
objections.why: The live DR-123 status cell reads '…(`COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md` D-009, CONSENT `cd08c5f0…`); evidence at DR-G01..G05/G12/G17'. The fenced lead target ends at the semicolon, so the evidence clause survives untouched, and I confirmed the omission mechanically rather than by impression: the string 'evidence at DR-G01..G05/G12/G17' occurs zero times inside clause 4 and once elsewhere in the subject, in the recitation that quotes it. So the entry has read that text, reasoned about it — Eligibility item 2 says 'After D-077, G17 is inapplicable (SARIF dropped from the preview)' — and elected not to repair it. Three things make that more than tidiness. First, the register already contradicts itself here and this entry deepens it: file 08's own DR-G17 gate row reads 'dropped / inapplicable (D-077 SARIF drop; D-086). not required-now', while DR-123's cells still route evidence there, and the Blueprint-impact replacement this entry writes adds 'G17 is inapplicable (D-077)' to the very same row. After adoption the row says both things at once, in adjacent columns. Second, gate 2 depends on it. The eligibility argument is that the remainder is only qualification evidence at DR-G01..G05 and DR-G12, and the sentence that would falsify that reading sits in the cell being written. Third, this is the ADV-D085-01 pattern, which the entry itself cites twice: a SATISFIED re-record must displace the stale execution-side statements in its own row rather than leave a reader to reconcile them. The source-pin column carries the same stale routing and belongs in the same repair. It is not a MUST-FIX because the staleness pre-dates this entry, the SATISFIED itself is not made false by it, and the row does carry the correction in the impact cell.
objections.repair: Extend the fenced lead replacement to cover the evidence clause — for example ending '…CONSENT `cd08c5f0…`); evidence at DR-G01..G05 and DR-G12; G17 inapplicable (D-077)' — or add a fourth exact edit for that clause, and consider the source-pin column in the same pass.

notesNonBlocking.observation: On adoption this exhausts D-056's authority. D-056 named exactly four rows 'eligible in kind, not performed' — DR-102, DR-115, DR-119, DR-123 — and D-085, D-089, D-091 and this entry perform all four. Nothing in the register will then authorize a fifth Class A or Class B re-record without a new eligibility decision, and D-056's ineligible table names DR-103/104/105/114/118 and the twelve no-contract rows explicitly. Recorded because the natural next question after four successful re-records is whether the pattern continues, and the answer is that it stops here until a successor amendment says otherwise. Condition 2 would stand at 4 of 30 and remain NOT MET, so no readiness threshold is approached by exhausting the set.

The attack 'lead replacement is not unique' fails, and the fencing repair from D-091 carries forward. I extracted all three fenced blocks byte-exactly from the draft: the lead target at 151 characters matches live file 08 at exactly one occurrence, and the two replacement texts at zero, which is correct for new text. The attack 'harness identifiers truncated or invented' fails, tested with the D091-SF-2 discipline. All four quoted identifiers appear in file 08 and each is a complete recorded identifier rather than a prefix, confirmed by matching each against its ' (D-086;' continuation: harness.DR-G01.core-download, harness.DR-G02.core-installed, harness.DR-G05.component-delta and harness.DR-G12.doctor-purge.preview. The set is also right — those are exactly the presently recordable required identifiers among DR-123's gates, since G03 and G04 are reserved and G17 is dropped.

The attack 'leftover is not only qualification' otherwise fails. D-009 records the baseline 'ACCEPTED as binding' across schemas, exit vocabulary, redaction, output-failure, offline operation and footprint, so what remains is execution and measurement of accepted obligations. DR-114 and DR-122 are live separate rows — DR-114 leads OPEN and DR-122 leads PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW — so 'remain other rows' is accurate for both, and TUI deferral to DR-129 matches the row's own 'not conditional on TUI scope' framing. G03/G04's unnamed state is placed on the same partition D-089 used and that D-006 authorises.

The attack 'D-085 / D-089 / D-091 remainders dropped from the snapshot' fails, established by fragment-by-fragment comparison of the live condition-2 cell against the fenced block. Every sentence of the live cell appears verbatim in the replacement — DR-102's CC-1..CC-11 leftover at DR-G21, DR-115's measurement leftover at DR-G01..G05, DR-119's TypeScript-role closure leftover at DR-G14, and DR-103's accepted-contract note — with the sole exception of the counts sentence. The block adds DR-123's own 'leftover CLI-baseline evidence remains at DR-G01..G05 and DR-G12 / condition 4', so all four satisfied rows name a remainder.

The counts verify against my own tally rather than either cell's assertion. The live lead-label tally over the thirty DR-1xx rows is 22 OPEN, 3 SATISFIED, 3 DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED and 2 PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW, summing to thirty, with DR-123 leading DECIDED. The target 'Hard blocker for **every** first blueprint slice; it is not conditional on TUI scope' is verbatim and unique, and the replacement displaces the hard-blocker while preserving the operative residue 'Not conditional on TUI scope.' — the clause that stops a later reader from reading the SATISFIED as contingent on TUI decisions.

objectionNote: I OBJECT with zero MUST-FIX and one SHOULD-FIX. This is the most disciplined draft of the four re-records — every finding from D-085, D-089 and D-091 arrives already applied, and each one verifies rather than merely appearing: the fenced target resolves to one live occurrence, the four identifiers are complete rather than prefixes, and the snapshot carries all three predecessors' remainders. I also checked the thing that looked wrong and was not, the CONSENT digest shared with D-008, which turns out to be one batch review serving both rows. The single objection is the one place the entry saw a problem and stopped short. It quotes 'evidence at DR-G01..G05/G12/G17' in its own eligibility recitation, explains that D-077 made G17 inapplicable, and then specifies no edit to that clause — I confirmed zero occurrences of it inside clause 4. The result would be a SATISFIED row routing evidence to a dropped gate in one column while the column next to it, written by this same entry, says the gate is inapplicable. That is the ADV-D085-01 pattern the entry cites twice in its own alternatives, and the repair is to extend a fenced replacement it has already written.
